study_identification_part.si_4_title: Extreme deviations from the normative model reveal cortical heterogeneity and associations with negative symptom severity in first-episode psychosis from the OPTiMiSE and GAP studies

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: OPTiMiSE multi-site FEP sample; GAP and ATLAS single-site samples (GAP patients and controls, plus ATLAS controls); pre-estimated multi-site reference normative model (n=37,126).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We included data from two large samples of individuals who were recruited and assessed at the time of their first presentation to services in the Genetics and Psychosis (GAP) study, and the Optimization of Treatment and Management of Schizophrenia in Europe (OPTiMiSE) study."; "As there were fewer control participants in the older age range in the GAP sample, additional data ( n = 124) from control participants in the ATLAS study were used to supplement the sample."; "We used a pre-estimated multi-site reference normative model... built from healthy participant data ( n = 37,126) across 79 scanners"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Participants, L43-L53; Worker2023.pdf.md: Participants, L49; Worker2023.pdf.md: Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L73-L78

answer.OPTiMiSE: FEP patients plus site controls; 50% of controls used for adaptation of the reference normative model, remaining controls and patients used as test samples for deviations

answer.SINGLE-SITE: GAP patients and controls; ATLAS controls used as the adaptation set for the GAP site; remaining GAP controls and patients used as test samples

answer.None (Pre-Trained NM): Pre-estimated multi-site reference normative model of cortical thickness used for model adaptation and deviation estimation

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: OPTiMiSE controls were split for adaptation (50%) and testing; GAP site used ATLAS controls for adaptation due to older-age representation; remaining controls and patients were test samples for deviation estimation against the reference model.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "the parameters of this reference normative model were adapted to the new sites with 50% of control participant data from each clinical site from the OPTiMiSE sample"; "ATLAS data was selected as the adaptation set..."; "For both samples, the remaining control participant and patient data were used as test samples for estimating deviations from the normative range."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L73-L78

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Reference normative model built from healthy participant data; no train/validation split reported.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "This model was built from healthy participant data ( n = 37,126) across 79 scanners"
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L73-L76

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Reference normative model age range reported as 6-100 years; no mean/sd reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "...multi-site MRI data with an age range of 6 -100 years"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex counts for the reference normative model were not reported; only that sex was modeled as a batch effect.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Participant sex and scanner site have been accounted for in the model by inclusion as batch effects"
